_comment: Hestia governance hooks for the AWS Kiro CLI occupant. Kiro CLI reads hooks from the 'hooks' field of a JSON AGENT CONFIG in .kiro/agents/<name>.json (project) or ~/.kiro/agents/<name>.json (global; local wins on name clash). Merge this 'hooks' block into the agent config you launch Kiro with. The IDE surface instead uses standalone JSON files in .kiro/hooks/ with fields version/name/trigger/matcher/action/timeout/enabled - see README for the IDE mapping. DOCUMENTED-tier: the exact entry schema (matcher/command/timeout key names) is from Kiro's hooks docs, not fired live; adjust per the installed CLI. The PreToolUse gate is FAIL-CLOSED (Kiro fails open, and exit 1 is a warning=ALLOW, so the gate carries a top-level deny-on-exception). It covers execute_bash + fs_write + use_aws + MCP calls; fs_read and other local reads pass scope but skip the governor. Commands bake HESTIA_WORKSPACE because the gate default (~/ai-workspace) is wrong on this host. HARDENING: install at GLOBAL/user level and put the scripts on ext4 (a 9p cold-load exceeding the 30s timeout fails OPEN); repoint the /mnt/c paths per install (a non-existent path spawn-errors into a fail-open).

PreToolUse._timeout_note: MILLISECONDS, at the engine default/maximum of 30s. Do NOT lower this. Kiro fails open on a hook timeout (the tool RUNS), so a shorter timeout strictly increases fail-open exposure and buys no safety - and the 9p cold-load warned about above is exactly the case that blows it. This was 15000 and is now 30000.
